_comment: The topic bank. The agent picks the least-recently-used topic each run (see src/state.js). Each topic is a brief that guides generation into the fixed carousel template: a cover, a context slide, exactly 3 teaching points, a recap, and a free-audit CTA. Edit freely, add more topics, or set "paused": true to skip one. Optional "theme" pins a palette (see templates/themes.js); otherwise palettes rotate least-recently-used.

topics.hook: 3 free things every local business can fix on Google today
topics.angle: Give away 3 real, do-it-today Google Business Profile fixes. Reciprocity: give the actual answers, do not withhold.
topics.targetKeyword: how to rank higher on Google Maps
points: Set the RIGHT primary category (most owners pick one too generic).
Fill out every single field on the profile (Google ranks complete profiles higher).
Post to your profile every week (active profiles get shown more).

topics.hook: Why the competitor with worse reviews outranks you
topics.angle: Counterintuitive myth-buster: it is not star count. Proximity, primary category, and profile completeness drive the map pack.
topics.targetKeyword: why do competitors rank higher on Google
points: Proximity to the searcher matters more than review count.
The right primary category beats a higher star rating.
A complete, active profile outranks a neglected one with more stars.

topics.hook: What the map pack is and why it is the only spot that matters for local
topics.angle: Pure education: define the local 3-pack, explain why being #7 in regular results is invisible on mobile.
topics.targetKeyword: what is the Google map pack
points: The map pack is the block of 3 businesses shown on the map.
Nearly all local clicks and calls go to those 3.
Ranking #7 in regular results is invisible to most mobile searchers.

topics.hook: I paid for SEO and it did not work. Here is what your last guy probably skipped
topics.angle: Objection handling with empathy. Most agencies chase backlinks and ignore the Google Business Profile, which is most of local ranking.
topics.targetKeyword: why did my SEO not work
points: Many agencies build backlinks and ignore your Google Business Profile.
For local, the profile and reviews drive most of the ranking.
Ask your provider what your primary category is. If they do not know, that is the problem.

topics.hook: The one Google Business Profile setting that quietly kills your ranking
topics.angle: High-curiosity single-point idea reframed as 3 checks. Deliver the real answer (wrong primary category / unverified / suspended).
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile ranking mistakes
points: A primary category that is too broad or simply wrong.
An unverified profile Google does not fully trust yet.
A profile flagged or suspended for guideline issues you never saw.

topics.hook: How to tell if your SEO company is actually doing anything
topics.angle: Position as the honest insider. Give 3 questions that a real provider answers instantly and a bad one cannot.
topics.targetKeyword: how to know if SEO is working
points: Ask: what is my primary Google Business Profile category?
Ask: how many local citations did you build or fix this month?
Ask: show me my current map-pack ranking for my main keyword.

topics.hook: Why page 1 in 7 days is a red flag, not a promise
topics.angle: Trust builder. Real local ranking takes 60 to 90 days. Instant promises mean risky tactics that get profiles suspended.
topics.targetKeyword: how long does local SEO take
points: Real local ranking movement takes about 60 to 90 days.
Anyone promising page 1 in days is using tactics that risk a suspension.
Sustainable ranking comes from the profile, reviews, and citations over time.

topics.hook: Rank your Google profile before you spend a dollar on a website
topics.angle: Contrarian sequencing. A ranked profile with calls beats a beautiful site nobody finds. (Keep it about sequence, not anti-website.)
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile vs website for local
points: A ranked Google profile brings calls even before a new website.
A website only converts the traffic you can already get found for.
Get the profile into the map pack first, then invest in the site.

topics.hook: The right way to ask for reviews so they actually help your ranking
topics.angle: Actionable how-to. Recent, keyword-mentioning, responded-to reviews help more than a big old pile.
topics.targetKeyword: how to get Google reviews that help ranking
points: Recency matters: a steady trickle beats one old burst.
Reviews that mention your service and city add ranking context.
Reply to every review. Google reads the engagement.

topics.hook: The free ranking factor most local businesses have never heard of: citations
topics.angle: Education plus a task. Consistent name, address, phone across directories builds trust with Google.
topics.targetKeyword: what are local citations for SEO
points: Citations are mentions of your name, address, and phone across the web.
Google trusts a business whose details match everywhere.
One wrong old phone number on a directory can quietly hurt you.

topics.hook: Replying to reviews is a ranking factor most owners skip
topics.angle: Actionable habit. Google reads engagement, and replies also convert readers who are still deciding.
topics.targetKeyword: should you reply to Google reviews
points: Reply to every review, good and bad, within a few days.
Use the service and city naturally in your reply, never stuffed.
A calm reply to a bad review sells better than a perfect rating.

topics.hook: The photos on your Google profile are doing more than you think
topics.angle: Most owners upload nothing or one logo. Fresh, real photos signal an active business.
topics.targetKeyword: do photos help Google Business Profile ranking
points: Upload real job photos, not stock images.
Add new photos every month so the profile looks active.
Cover the basics: exterior, interior, team, and finished work.

topics.hook: How to write a Google Business Profile description that actually helps
topics.angle: The 750 character description is free real estate almost everyone wastes.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile description examples
points: Lead with what you do and where you do it.
Name your main services in the plain language customers use.
Skip slogans and awards, Google ignores them.

topics.hook: Setting your service area wrong is quietly capping your reach
topics.angle: Service area businesses get this backwards constantly, either far too broad or far too narrow.
topics.targetKeyword: how to set service area Google Business Profile
points: List the cities you truly serve, not the whole state.
Too wide a radius dilutes your relevance in every city.
Hide your address only if customers never visit you.

topics.hook: You might have a second Google listing you never created
topics.angle: Duplicates split reviews and confuse Google. Very common after a move or a rebrand.
topics.targetKeyword: duplicate Google Business Profile
points: Search your business name and phone number on Google Maps.
Duplicates split reviews and ranking signals between listings.
Claim and merge them through the profile support flow.

topics.hook: One wrong phone number on an old directory can hurt your ranking
topics.angle: Name, address, and phone consistency. Boring but real.
topics.targetKeyword: NAP consistency local SEO
points: Your name, address, and phone must match everywhere online.
Old listings with a former number or suite confuse Google.
Fix the biggest directories first, then work down the list.

topics.hook: The Google profile button that sends leads straight to your phone
topics.angle: Messaging is off by default on most profiles. A free lead channel sitting unused.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile messaging
points: Turn on messaging so customers can text you from search.
Set an away reply so nobody gets silence.
Slow replies get the feature disabled, so answer fast.

topics.hook: Anyone can answer questions on your Google profile, including competitors
topics.angle: The Q and A section is public and unmoderated. Owners should seed it themselves.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile questions and answers
points: Anyone can post and answer questions on your listing.
Seed your own common questions and answer them yourself.
Check the section monthly for wrong or hostile answers.

topics.hook: Why stuffing keywords into your business name can get you suspended
topics.angle: It works until it does not. An honest warning about a common shady tactic.
topics.targetKeyword: keyword stuffing Google Business Profile name
points: Your listed name must match your real world signage.
Competitors and Google both report stuffed names.
A suspension costs far more than the temporary bump.

topics.hook: Wrong hours on Google cost you more customers than bad reviews
topics.angle: A simple trust and ranking factor, especially around holidays.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile hours
points: Set real hours and update them for every holiday.
A locked door when Google says open earns instant one star reviews.
Special hours fields exist for a reason, use them.

topics.hook: The products section works even if you do not sell products
topics.angle: Service businesses can list services as products for extra visibility.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile products section
points: Service businesses can list each service as a product.
Each entry gets its own photo, price range, and description.
It gives you more indexed text tied to your profile.

topics.hook: If you cannot tell where your calls come from, you cannot fix anything
topics.angle: Measurement basics. Ties directly into the free audit offer.
topics.targetKeyword: how to track Google Business Profile leads
points: Your profile shows calls, clicks, and direction requests.
Tag your website link so profile traffic shows up separately.
Ask every caller how they found you, and write it down.

topics.hook: A slow website quietly drags down your local ranking
topics.angle: An on-page factor that supports the map pack, not just the blue links.
topics.targetKeyword: does website speed affect local SEO
points: Most local searches happen on phones with average connections.
Oversized images are the top cause of slow local sites.
A page that takes several seconds loses the customer and the ranking.

topics.hook: Why one page cannot rank you in five different cities
topics.angle: Explains dedicated location pages, the fix most small sites are missing.
topics.targetKeyword: local landing pages for multiple cities
points: Google needs a distinct page for each city you want to rank in.
Each page needs genuinely different content, not a swapped city name.
Thin copied pages get ignored or penalized.

topics.hook: The invisible code that tells Google exactly what your business is
topics.angle: Local business schema, explained without the jargon.
topics.targetKeyword: local business schema markup
points: Schema is hidden code that labels your name, address, and hours.
It helps Google connect your website to your Google profile.
Most small business sites have none of it.

topics.hook: Not all Google posts are the same, and one of them gets ignored
topics.angle: Practical breakdown of update, offer, and event post types.
topics.targetKeyword: types of Google Business Profile posts
points: Update posts are the workhorse, use them weekly.
Offer posts show a highlighted banner and a date range.
Event posts expire, so do not rely on them for evergreen info.

topics.hook: The review tactic that violates Google policy and gets you removed
topics.angle: Review gating. Honest, protective advice that builds trust.
topics.targetKeyword: is review gating against Google policy
points: Screening out unhappy customers before asking is against policy.
Ask every customer the same way, every time.
Removed reviews and a flagged profile are the penalty.

topics.hook: What actually happens when a business buys Google reviews
topics.angle: Cautionary. Positions EPG as the honest operator.
topics.targetKeyword: buying Google reviews consequences
points: Google detects unnatural review bursts and strips them.
Repeat offenses can disable the profile entirely.
Real reviews from real jobs are slower and permanent.

topics.hook: How to reverse engineer the competitor sitting above you
topics.angle: Teaches a real audit workflow using only free tools.
topics.targetKeyword: how to analyze local SEO competitors
points: Open their profile and note the primary category.
Compare review count, recency, and reply rate against yours.
Check which fields they filled that you left blank.

topics.hook: The honest truth about ranking in a city you are not near
topics.angle: Manages expectations. Proximity is the one factor nobody can buy.
topics.targetKeyword: can I rank in a city I am not located in
points: Proximity to the searcher is a major map pack factor.
You can widen your reach, but you cannot fake a location.
Service area pages and citations help more than address tricks.

topics.hook: An unverified Google profile is barely a profile at all
topics.angle: Verification basics and what to do when it fails.
topics.targetKeyword: how to verify Google Business Profile
points: Unverified profiles rank poorly and can be edited by strangers.
Video verification is now the most common method.
Have signage, tools, and your workspace ready before you record.

topics.hook: Should a local business run Google Ads or fix their SEO first?
topics.angle: An honest comparison that does not trash ads. Builds credibility.
topics.targetKeyword: local SEO vs Google Ads
points: Ads buy instant visibility that stops when the budget stops.
Local SEO builds slower but keeps working after you stop paying.
A broken profile makes your ads more expensive too.

topics.hook: Call tracking numbers can wreck your local ranking if set up wrong
topics.angle: A specific technical gotcha most owners never hear about.
topics.targetKeyword: call tracking numbers and local SEO
points: A tracking number replacing your real number breaks consistency.
Keep your real number as the primary everywhere.
Use the secondary number field for tracking instead.

topics.hook: The free listing almost every local business forgets
topics.angle: Bing Places, plus why it matters more now that AI assistants pull from it.
topics.targetKeyword: Bing Places for Business
points: Bing powers results in places most people never think about.
Setup takes minutes and can import straight from Google.
It is one more consistent citation pointing at your business.

topics.hook: Every iPhone user searching nearby is using a map you probably ignored
topics.angle: Apple Business Connect. Genuinely overlooked and an easy win.
topics.targetKeyword: Apple Business Connect listing
points: iPhone users searching nearby often see Apple Maps first.
Apple Business Connect is free to claim and edit.
An unclaimed listing may show wrong hours or a wrong pin.

topics.hook: You do not need 200 directory listings, you need the right ones
topics.angle: Cuts through citation spam services. Quality over quantity.
topics.targetKeyword: best local citation directories
points: A handful of major data sources feed most smaller directories.
Industry specific directories carry more weight than generic ones.
Consistency across a few beats sloppiness across hundreds.

topics.hook: Your customers are judging your business on a phone screen
topics.angle: Mobile experience as both a conversion and a ranking issue.
topics.targetKeyword: mobile friendly local business website
points: Most local searches and calls happen on a phone.
Your phone number should be tappable on every page.
If they have to pinch and zoom, they leave.

topics.hook: Your Google profile already tells you what is broken, if you read it
topics.angle: Teaches how to interpret the performance tab. Ties into the free audit.
topics.targetKeyword: Google Business Profile insights explained
points: Compare how many people found you by name versus by category.
Mostly name searches means you are not being discovered.
Track calls and direction requests month over month, not daily.

topics.hook: The seasonal ranking window most local businesses miss entirely
topics.angle: Timing. You must already be ranking before the season starts.
topics.targetKeyword: seasonal local SEO
points: Ranking takes weeks, so prepare a full season ahead.
Update services and posts before demand spikes, not after.
Seasonal photos and offers keep the profile relevant.

topics.hook: That competitor with the fake address can be removed
topics.angle: Empowering and a little satisfying. A tool most owners never heard of.
topics.targetKeyword: how to report a fake Google Business listing
points: Fake addresses and keyword stuffed names violate guidelines.
Google has a redressal form for reporting them.
Removing a spam listing can move you up a spot immediately.
